Who this practice is for

This short refresher is for introductory university mathematics and students returning to two- and three-dimensional vectors. Because it includes the cross product, it is not presented as ordinary GCSE vector practice.

Four practice pages contain quick reminders, examples and ten questions, including one optional scaling challenge. Two pages of worked answers explain all ten solutions. The publication copy clarifies the non-zero-vector and zero-cross-product cases.

6 pages · 10 questions · Aim: 20 minutes · Worked answers

Topics covered

  • Vectors between two points
  • Magnitude and unit vectors
  • Dot product and perpendicularity of non-zero vectors
  • Three-dimensional cross product
  • Scaling a vector to a required magnitude

Prerequisites: basic algebra, coordinates, vector components and square roots. This is a short skills refresher, not a complete vector course or an exam paper. The 20-minute target is a flexible practice aim; it includes one optional challenge.

Key ideas at a glance

Normalise only a non-zero vector

Divide a vector by its magnitude to obtain a unit vector in the same direction, provided the original vector is non-zero. The zero vector has no direction and cannot be normalised.

Distinguish scalar and vector products

The dot product is a scalar; for two non-zero vectors, a zero dot product means perpendicular directions. A non-zero cross product is a vector perpendicular to both inputs. Parallel inputs, or a zero input, give the zero vector with no direction.
